system: You are an ambitious AI PhD student in computational genomics who is looking to publish a paper that will contribute significantly to the field.
task_description: You are given a validation experiment that tests whether Evo2-7B embeddings encode functional gene class information beyond the specific DNA repair vs tumor suppressor contrast studied in prior work. This experiment uses a completely different functional contrast: glycolysis genes (KEGG hsa00010, metabolic pathway) vs T-cell receptor signaling genes (KEGG hsa04660, immune signaling pathway). These two classes are biologically unrelated to DNA repair or cancer suppression. A frozen Evo2-7B model extracts mean-pooled embeddings from layer blocks.28.mlp.l3, and a shallow MLP classifier (256->128->1) is trained to distinguish the two classes. The prior experiment (DNA repair vs TSG) achieved 0.78 AUROC. The validation question is: does a similar AUROC hold for this completely different functional contrast, and what does the comparison tell us about how broadly Evo2 encodes functional information? IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS: (1) Do NOT add new gene classes — use only glycolysis and T-cell signaling. (2) Reuse cached dataset.json and embeddings from run_0/data/. (3) Focus experiments on probing the geometry, linear separability, and layer-dependence of the functional signal.
